s1.meaning: a conversion's mean time with nothing else running, the service's HTTP work around it included and the client's transfer not: the CPU's speed for this workload (lower is faster; 0.94 on a Xeon Gold 6248R vCPU)

contention.meaning: how much slower a conversion runs with every vCPU converting at once: the memory bus and the caches (1.10 on the M1, 1.18 on the Xeon)

disk_mbps.meaning: the disk's sustained write rate under /tmp, 1 MiB direct writes; null if not measured (IOPS do not matter: a conversion writes ~50 writes of ~0.9 MB)

workload.name: report
workload.meaning: what this document mix costs on any hardware (measured equal on arm64 and amd64)

limits.meaning: what bounds a conversion whatever the document: the hard memory limit an instance is killed above, how far past it one 100 ms read lets it get, and what a conversion leaves in /tmp

formulas.why: one conversion uses one core; a larger pool adds no throughput and slows each conversion, a smaller one leaves cores idle

formulas.what: a conversion's time with every instance busy

formulas.formula: X_cpu = min(POOL_SIZE, vCPU) / S_sat conversions/s (× 60 a minute)

formulas.what: throughput, disk-bound (/tmp on disk; none on a tmpfs)
formulas.here: 0.459 × B / 28.2: e.g. a 120 MB/s SATA SSD gives 1.96/s

formulas.what: a conversion's time: the floor (alone) and at saturation
formulas.formula: p_q = s1 × time_quantiles_over_mean[q] alone, S_sat × time_quantiles_over_mean[q] busy
formulas.here: alone p50 2.6 s, p95 3.3 s, p99 3.6 s; busy p50 3.1 s, p95 3.9 s, p99 4.2 s; no hardware beats the floor

formulas.formula: memory_service_mib + POOL_SIZE × (hard_memory_mib + hard_memory_overshoot_mib) + tmpfs MiB, tmpfs = the /tmp size below if /tmp is a tmpfs, else 0: every instance at the hard limit at once, so no document mix can OOM the pod; set hard_memory_mib to DOCX_TO_PDF_INSTANCE_HARD_MEMORY if it is not the default
formulas.here: 256 + 4 × (2048 + 256) = 9472 MiB on disk, 10626 MiB with a tmpfs of 1154 MiB

formulas.what: memory limit for the typical mix only (a named option)
formulas.formula: (1 + memory_headroom) × (memory_service_mib + memory_per_instance_mib × POOL_SIZE + tmpfs) MiB, tmpfs = tmpfs_per_pool_slot_mib × POOL_SIZE if /tmp is a tmpfs, else 0: fitted on the workload's documents; a heavier document (many tables, gigapixel pictures) can OOM the pod, and with memory.oom.group the OOM kills every conversion in it
formulas.here: 1.25 × (256 + 256 × 4) = 1600 MiB on disk, 1920 MiB with a tmpfs of 256 MiB

formulas.what: the pool a memory limit R MiB allows
formulas.formula: floor((R - memory_service_mib - tmpfs) / (hard_memory_mib + hard_memory_overshoot_mib)); for the typical mix floor((R / (1 + memory_headroom) - memory_service_mib - tmpfs) / memory_per_instance_mib)

formulas.what: /tmp size (an emptyDir sizeLimit, or the tmpfs)
formulas.formula: (POOL_SIZE + 1) × profile_mib + POOL_MAX_WAITING × D + POOL_SIZE × max(tmp_documents_per_conversion × D, tmp_long_layout_mib) MiB, rounded up, D = DOCX_TO_PDF_MAX_DOCUMENT_SIZE in MiB; a deflate bomb is refused once its parts inflate past DOCX_TO_PDF_MAX_INFLATED_SIZE, max(3 × D, 256 MiB) by default
POOL_MAX_WAITING = POOL_SIZE; CONVERSION_TIMEOUT = max(180 s, 4 × busy p99); POOL_WAIT_TIMEOUT = max(30 s, 1.5 × (POOL_MAX_WAITING / POOL_SIZE + 1) × busy p99), both rounded up to 10 s
formulas.here: DOCX_TO_PDF_POOL_SIZE=4, DOCX_TO_PDF_POOL_MAX_WAITING=4, DOCX_TO_PDF_CONVERSION_TIMEOUT=180s, DOCX_TO_PDF_POOL_WAIT_TIMEOUT=30s, DOCX_TO_PDF_INSTANCE_MAX_MEMORY=1024MiB, DOCX_TO_PDF_INSTANCE_HARD_MEMORY=2048MiB, DOCX_TO_PDF_MAX_DOCUMENT_SIZE=32MiB

formulas.what: response time at an open rate λ requests/s on one pod (an M/G/c queue)
formulas.formula: ρ = λ × s1 / (POOL_SIZE - λ × (S_sat - s1)); E[S] = s1 + (S_sat - s1) × ρ; a = λ × E[S] (must stay below POOL_SIZE); P_wait = Erlang C(POOL_SIZE, a) = (a^c / c!) × c / (c - a) / (Σ_{i<c} a^i / i! + (a^c / c!) × c / (c - a)), c = POOL_SIZE; the wait is P_wait × an exponential of rate θ = (POOL_SIZE / E[S] - λ) × 2 / (c_a² + service_time_cv2), c_a² = 1 for independent clients; response = wait + E[S] × time_quantiles_over_mean, its quantile solved numerically (bench.py size target)

formulas.what: pods for a rate R and a response-time target
formulas.formula: pods = ceil(R / (0.85 × X)), then one more while the target quantile at R / pods exceeds the target; add one for N+1
formulas.here: R = 60/min, p95 ≤ 10 s: 1 pod(s) of 4 vCPU
